To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the distribution of carbofuran residues in a rice‐plant ecosystem is as follows: (i) The parent compound is readily absorbed from the soil and distributed to the different parts of the rice plants; (ii) The concentration of carbofuron in rice plant was found to be 10‐15 times higher than the concentration in water; and (iii) The concentration of 14 C‐carbofuron in fish was found to be very low, indicating its low bioaccumulation
the distribution of carbofuran residues in a rice‐plant‐fish system was studied over a 90‐day period and that carbofuron did not accumulate to any appreciable extent in fish.
carbofuron is rapidly metabolized in the rice plant to 3‐hydroxycarbofuran and 3‐ketocarbofuran, both of which are readily absorbed by the fish.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the fate of 14C-carbofuran in rice-fish model ecosystem.
the distribution and fate of 14C-Carbofuran residues in a model rice-fish ecosystem.
the fate of the insecticide carbofuran in rice‐fish model ecosystems and its distribution in different constituents of the ecosystem.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
carbofuron residues are not likely to persist in rice‐fish model ecosystems.
the residues of 14C-carbofuran in the different components of a model rice-fish ecosystem decreased rapidly with time.
carbofurna is readily metabolized by the plant, soil and fish, with the parent compound contributing only about 10% to the total residue after 30 days in all cases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
carbofuron is readily absorbed by the plant and distributed to all plant parts and is also readily absorbed by the fish.
the rice plants contained the largest amount of 14C-residues and the fish contained the lowest amount of residues.
14C‐ carbofuran was absorbed by rice plant, and the residues were distributed to different parts of the plant.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of carbofuran is not recommended in rice cultivation as a result of its high toxicity to aquatic organisms.

the fate of carbofuran in rice‐fish ecosystem is similar to the fate of carfofuran in soil‐plant systems and the residues of carfofuron in the ecosystem are not likely to pose any risk to human health and aquatic environment.
the fate of carbofuran in the rice‐fish model system is not very different from its behaviour in other ecosystems.
